title: Chirurgie des surfaces conformes : notes manuscrites (s.d., 1983-1984), lettres (1984).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is part of an English letter (pages numbered 4-5 of the letter) about the 'surgery' that relates compact conformal surfaces with boundary to compact surfaces with marked points. Take X compact conformal with boundary. Give it its unique hyperbolic metric with geodesic boundary. Each boundary circle then carries a rotation action (arc-length mod length). Cap each boundary circle with a disc whose rotation action matches. The result is a closed surface X^ with points s_i and disjoint discs D_i around them. Discs may be degenerate, i.e. reduced to the point s_i, which corresponds to cusps. A disc system obtained this way is called 'admissible'. Let MB be the moduli (Teichmüller-type) space of bordered surfaces and M that of punctured ones. Then MB fibres over M, and the fibre over (X^, s_i) is the set of admissible disc systems.

This page parametrises the fibre by 'radii'. A conformal disc D with interior point s embeds canonically in T_s as the unit disc of a hermitian norm. Concretely, compose the Riemann map phi: D -> unit disc, phi(s)=0, with dphi_s^{-1}; the result is independent of rotations. This is the conformal radius. So the radius at s_i is a point of an R^{+*}-torsor R_i, completed by radius 0 to R_i^, and a system of discs gives r in prod R_i^.

Grothendieck makes two expectations. (1) An admissible system is determined by r. (2) The realisable r form a product region r_i < rho_i for some fixed rho. He notes himself that (2) conflicts with his earlier hoped-for action of (P^{≠})^I on MB~, unless all rho_i = +infinity.

He then reduces to the key case of Thurston's pants. X^ is the Riemann sphere with 0, 1, infinity placed equidistantly on the equator. The sphere is cut into three 'orange slices' Q_i by three half great circles joining the poles P+ and P-, each half circle equidistant from two of the points. The next page proposes the model: admissible triples are exactly (lambda_i Q_i), 0 <= lambda_i < 1, where lambda Q_i is the 'concentric' shrinking of Q_i in its conformal disc structure. Consequences he draws: MB~ ≅ M~ × [0,1[^I; the intersection of all pants would be the three half circles; the two poles would be intrinsic invariants of a pair of pants.
errors: The orange-slice model (stated here, made explicit on the next page) appears to be false; the argument relies on standard limit theorems rather than a full proof. Take ell_2 = ell_3 = 0 (cusps at s_2, s_3) and ell_1 -> infinity. The hyperbolic surface has fixed area 2π and a long geodesic boundary, so it becomes thin. Conformally, the complement of D_1 then converges to the critical graph of the Jenkins–Strebel differential with a double pole at s_1 and simple poles at s_2, s_3: the equatorial arc from s_2 to s_3 avoiding s_1. Hence for large ell_1 the poles P± lie inside D_1. But P± lie on the boundary of Q_1, so D_1 cannot equal any lambda_1 Q_1.

For the same reason, the claim that 'the intersection of all [pants] would be the three half circles' fails. As all ell_i -> infinity, the limiting spine is the Strebel ribbon graph for the ratio (ell_0 : ell_1 : ell_\infty). Its shape depends on the ratio: a theta graph when the triangle inequalities hold, otherwise a different trivalent graph. The three half circles with vertices P± occur only in the equal-ratio case.

In the model, the shape of D_i depends only on lambda_i. This is implausible: changing D_j changes the hyperbolic metric on the complement, hence the arc-length action on the boundary of D_i. Grothendieck himself suspects something like this on the next page regarding ell_i.
The product-region expectation r_i < rho_i for conformal radii is unsupported, and he himself notes it is inconsistent with his earlier expectation.

ideas.what: Admissibility of disc systems: the circle action from the conformal disc must agree with the arc-length action from the geodesic boundary of the hyperbolic complement. This lets surfaces with boundary be viewed as punctured surfaces plus disc data.
ideas.modern_name: Capping/filling bordered hyperbolic surfaces; fibration of bordered Teichmüller space over punctured Teichmüller space
ideas.usually_credited_to: Various (e.g. Mondello's work on surfaces with boundary and ribbon graphs, 2000s); no single standard credit
ideas.where_published: Possibly alluded to in Esquisse d'un programme (1984) discussion of Teichmüller tower / surgery; unsure

ideas.what: Radius of a disc around s as a hermitian norm on T_s (canonical embedding of a pointed conformal disc into the tangent space); radii form an R^{+*}-torsor.
ideas.modern_name: Conformal radius / capacity as a norm on the tangent line

ideas.what: Orange-slice decomposition of P^1 with 0, 1, infinity equidistant on the equator; three half great circles meeting at the two poles proposed as intrinsic invariants of pants.
ideas.modern_name: Critical graph of the Jenkins–Strebel differential with equal residues at 0, 1, infinity (theta ribbon graph; zeros at the order-3 fixed points); spine of hyperbolic pants
ideas.usually_credited_to: Strebel (Quadratic Differentials, 1984); Harer–Mumford–Thurston/Penner/Kontsevich ribbon-graph cell decompositions (1986–92); Bowditch–Epstein spine (1988)
ideas.where_published: Related ribbon-graph/dessin ideas appear in Esquisse d'un programme (1984), but not this specific model as far as I know

ideas.what: Conjectured product structure MB~ ≅ M~ × [0,1[^I (made explicit on the next page).
ideas.modern_name: Trivialisation of the bordered-to-punctured Teichmüller fibration

missed.claim: Grothendieck's guessed 'limiting' configuration for pants is exactly the equal-residue Jenkins–Strebel critical graph on P^1 minus {0, 1, infinity}: a theta graph whose two vertices are the poles. He wonders whether these poles and half circles are intrinsically attached to a pant. This anticipates the later picture: hyperbolic surfaces with boundary lengths tending to infinity degenerate to metric ribbon graphs (Strebel graphs), and the pants have intrinsic spines with two trivalent vertices (Bowditch–Epstein; Mondello; Do). These later developments explain why his model fails off the equal-ratio ray.
missed.quote: These points may be viewed as the centers of three "orange slices", making up a cellular subdivision of Σ
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historically, this is a 1983–84 instance of Grothendieck reaching for ribbon-graph/Strebel structures from the hyperbolic-surgery side, parallel to Harer–Mumford–Thurston. Mathematically it is superseded, and the specific model is wrong.

missed.claim: He asks for an intrinsic description of the space of admissible disc systems on a pointed Riemann surface, i.e. the fibre of bordered over punctured moduli, in terms of conformal radii, and conjectures it is a product of intervals. The precise shape of this image in conformal-radius coordinates seems not to be worked out explicitly in the literature, as far as I know.
missed.quote: a given set of radii corresponds to an admissible system of discs iff it satisfies a set of unequalities r_i < ρ_i
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a concrete, checkable question about the capping map for bordered hyperbolic surfaces, but of modest interest.

deep.surprise_reason: This is an interesting letter-draft glimpse of Grothendieck attacking bordered/punctured Teichmüller theory via conformal radii and an 'orange slice' model of pants. The model coincides with the equal-length Strebel/ribbon-graph limit, but it is false in general, and the correct picture was developed independently later. It is a notable but not groundbreaking unpublished detail.
transcription_corrections: 'uncer' is a typo in the typescript for 'under'.
The handwritten insertion after 'set' (twice) replacing the struck typed '#' looks like a hatted 'r' (the radius vector r), not 'Γ'.
'where equal to + ∞' is the original's typo for 'were equal'.
Line 4: the typed word is overstruck and replaced by handwritten 'over'.
